item.title: GovBrief Today #577
item.description: Donald Trump asked the FCC to punish a journalist for doubting him. Kristen Welker reported on NBC that his primary endorsement record was mixed. Six of his candidates lost Republican primaries in August. Trump called her a "Hostess," accused her of "purposeful inaccuracy," and said she would be reported to the FCC "for rebuke or punishment." In June she interviewed him in a Wisconsin barn and asked for evidence of his claim that California was rigging its primary count. He told her "you're either crooked or you're stupid," said he'd had enough, and walked out with "Thank you, darling." He handled that one himself. Now he wants FCC Chair Brendan Carr to handle it for him. I've emailed 8,882 stories over 577 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you. item.title: Race as a construct: busting medical myths with Dr. Joel Bervell
item.description:
Dr. Joel Bervell is an award winning trailblazer in clinical science communication. In addition to his practice he has built a science communication channel focusing on racial disparities in clinical care. Here he analyses two twins that could be considered different races despite being siblings from the same parents.
Responding to race as a social construct. Social construct does not mean imaginary. Race impacts are very real. When we think of skincare, hair care, economic conditions, treatment by police, we see clear delineations of racial impacts.
The history of the construction of race is wild to dive into. Standard repost disclosures: I am NOT Joel Bervell, he is found on yt, ig, tt, @joelbervell to follow, support, and engage with
